chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhassin from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the locust, whether the Muhrim (one in Ihram) may eat it. He said, 'No.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim in the state of Ihram eat locusts?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that locusts are among the few exceptions to the general prohibition of hunting or consuming game while in the state of Ihram. This ruling highlights the distinction between wild game (which is forbidden) and locusts, which are treated more like permissible land animals or insects, allowing the Muhrim to eat them without incurring a penalty.
